title: Shhh! France's President Tells a Whole Room to Be Quiet
summary:
Have you ever been in a room where everyone is chatting so loudly that nobody can hear the speaker? That's what happened at a big meeting in Nairobi, Kenya, but the speaker was the president of France!

President Emmanuel Macron was at the Africa Forward summit, where leaders from more than 30 African countries, business people, and young entrepreneurs were talking about working together. But while someone was speaking on stage, the audience kept having their own conversations. Macron got so frustrated that he interrupted the speaker to tell everyone to be quiet.

"There is a total lack of respect," Macron said. He told people that if they wanted to keep talking, they should go outside or find a meeting room. The French leader is in Kenya to strengthen friendships and business ties between France and African countries.

The summit was a big deal, but the noise made it hard to focus. Imagine if you were giving a presentation in class and your classmates wouldn't stop whispering—you'd probably want the teacher to step in. That's basically what Macron did, except he's the president!

The rest of the news that day was full of other stories—like a ceasefire between the US and Iran, a missing American pilot, and a plan for a detention center in Georgia. But the moment everyone was talking about was a president shushing a room full of grown-ups.
why_it_matters: Just like in a classroom, if everyone talks while someone is presenting, nothing gets learned—important meetings need quiet attention so countries can solve problems together.

background_read: President Emmanuel Macron (the leader of France) was at a big meeting in Nairobi, the capital city of Kenya, where African and international leaders talk about working together.
Summits like Africa Forward bring together governments and young business starters to discuss ideas, but side conversations can make it hard for everyone to listen and learn.
France has a long history with many African countries, and today it tries to build friendly business and cultural connections there.

perspectives.description: Some people think Macron did the right thing by insisting on respect, which helps important meetings work properly.
Others feel that shaming grown-ups publicly was rude and could damage friendships between France and African partners.
